question: When a product-wiring acceptance receipt names a workflow run, does this repository still hold the gate's own verdict for that run?
answer: Usually not. 88 distinct runs are named by a live record; 8 of them have an on-disk verdict under raster-runs/. 221 wiring receipts rest on a run whose verdict this repository does not retain.
whatThisIsNot: NOT fabrication. FIX170 reported one of these as a receipt naming a run 'this repository holds no raster record for', which was accurate about raster-runs/ and easy to read as a phantom. Three of the least-referenced run ids were checked against GitHub directly -- 34297296663 (run 139), 33977133323 (run 77) and 33590575410 (run 22) -- and all three are real RCAP Packet Raster Acceptance (batch) runs that completed with conclusion success. The receipts name real runs.
whatThisIs: A durability gap. The receipt is ingested from the run's log, the queue carries a summary, and the gate's own verdict document is retained on disk for only a few runs. A reader who checks raster-runs/ for the other 80 finds nothing and cannot tell a real acceptance from an invented one without leaving the repository.
whyItMatters: GitHub Actions artifacts and run logs age out. Once they do, a wiring receipt naming an unretained run has no backing anywhere -- not in the repository, not upstream. 175 of the families currently COMPLETE_PACKET_PROVEN rest on such a receipt.
theCure: Ingestion should write the gate's verdict document to raster-runs/ for every admitted run, not only for runs whose artifact happened to be downloaded. That is a change to ingest-raster-receipt.mjs and is not made here.
decidesNothing: No family is demoted, no receipt withdrawn and no verdict changed by this record.
